decision_conditions: The applicant has not provided accurate information regarding the proposed development, specifically in relation to site levels and the relationship/ interaction with the existing rear garage. Furthermore, there are inconsistencies between the submitted floor and elevation plans. As a result, the proposal cannot be fully assessed against relevant design and amenity policies, including London Plan policies D3 and D4, Enfield Core Strategy policy CP30, and Enfield Development Management Document policies DMD6 and DMD11. Consequently, the proposal is contrary to Planning Practice Guidance, the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), and The Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015.

Having regard to reason for refusal 1, the proposal has failed to demonstrate that it would not have an unacceptable impact on the residential amenities of the occupiers of number 23 Grange Park Avenue through loss of outlook, overdominance and a heightened sense of enclosure. The proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD11 and DMD37 of the Development Management Document (2014).

Having regard to reason for refusal 1, the proposal has failed to demonstrate that it would not have unacceptable impact on the character and appearance of the existing house or the pattern of development in the immediate area due to its excessive overall depth, and its design (particularly its physical relationship with the existing garage). The proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD6, DMD11 and DMD37 of the Development Management Document (2014).
